history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: Chabimura is NOT at Ambassa - the CSV town is WRONG. Chabimura (also Chakwrakma/Chakrakma) is the rock-carving site on the steep mountain walls of Devtamura (Debtamura) on the bank of the Gomati river at Haakwchak/Haakchak, in Amarpur subdivision, Gomati district - 82 km from Agartala, 30 km from Udaipur and 7.5-12 km from Amarpur. Ambassa is the Dhalai district HQ ~90 km away and is wrong. Documented with the corrected nearest town Amarpur. The carvings: huge images of Shiva, Vishnu, Kartika, Mahishasurmardini Durga and other gods/goddesses etched on near-vertical (90-degree) sandstone faces of the Kalajhari hills that drain into the Gomati; 37 rock-cut images per Wikipedia; the biggest is the ~20-ft (Tripura Tourism: 10.7 m high x 7.7 m wide) ten-armed Mahishasurmardini relief called Chakrak Ma by local tribes, one of the largest Durga reliefs in the country. Purpose and artists unknown; the site is reached only by motorboat/canoe along the Gomati gorge followed by forest trekking, and the area is an eco-tourism centre. An annual mid-January fair is held at the Damburu Falls terraces on Devtamura. town_description: Amarpur is a subdivision town in Gomati district, Tripura, ~82 km southeast of Agartala and ~30 km from Udaipur. It is the gateway to the Chabimura/Devtamura rock carvings on the Gomati river (boat ride from near Amarpur), Damburu Falls, and Tripura's 'Amazon' gorge corridor.
